question: What is the Sibling Scholarship Scheme?
answer: The Sibling Scholarship Scheme provides a 20% reduction in tuition fees for an immediate sibling of a current or former Asansol Engineering College student. The programmes listed are BBA, BCA, MCA, B.Tech and M.Tech. Proof of the sibling relationship is required. The policy allocates 5% of the approved intake, on a first-come, first-served basis. These details were published in the 2024-25 policy, so current availability and rules should be reconfirmed with AEC.

question: What is the Employee Scholarship Scheme and how much is the scholarship?
answer: The Employee Scholarship Scheme is for eligible children or immediate siblings of permanent AEC employees who meet the service requirements. The tuition-fee scholarship is 10% for 3-5 years of continuous service, 15% for more than 5 and up to 10 years, 25% for more than 10 and up to 15 years, and 40% for more than 15 years. The employee must have at least three years of continuous service as of 30 June of the relevant academic session. Only one child or immediate sibling of the employee may receive the benefit. The listed programmes are BBA, BCA, MCA, B.Tech and M.Tech. The policy was published for 2024-25; obtain current confirmation from AEC.

question: What is the Alumni Scholarship Scheme?
answer: The Alumni Scholarship Scheme provides a 20% reduction in tuition fees to an AEC graduate admitted to a second degree programme at AEC. The transitions specifically listed are BCA to MCA and B.Tech to M.Tech. The policy limits the allocation to 5% of the approved intake on a first-come, first-served basis. Current availability should be reconfirmed with AEC.

question: What is the B.Tech Topper Scholarship for M.Tech?
answer: The scholarship provides a full tuition-fee waiver to the four-year B.Tech topper of any stream at AEC who chooses to pursue M.Tech at AEC. The policy was published for the 2024-25 session. Current topper-selection rules and eligibility should be confirmed with the college.

question: What is the Core Branch Scholarship?
answer: The Core Branch Scholarship provides ₹10,000 per semester for the listed B.Tech programmes: Civil Engineering, Mechanical Engineering and Electrical Engineering. Eligibility routes include WBJEE or JEE Main rank. Diploma-to-B.Tech lateral-entry students in these branches with a JELET rank are also listed. The policy describes an allocation of 5% of the approved intake for top rank holders. The current rank cut-off and application process are not confirmed and should be checked with AEC.

question: What is the Swami Vivekananda Merit-cum-Means Scholarship (SVMCM)?
answer: SVMCM provides financial assistance to meritorious students from economically weaker families in West Bengal. Typical undergraduate engineering eligibility includes West Bengal domicile, at least 60% in the qualifying examination and annual family income not exceeding ₹2.5 lakh, subject to applicable rules. For postgraduate engineering, the stated guideline requires at least 55% in graduation for the engineering or technology category. The published scholarship rate is ₹5,000 per month for eligible undergraduate engineering, postgraduate engineering and other listed AICTE-approved professional courses. Renewal depends on satisfactory academic performance, passing examinations and submitting renewal documents. Common documents include qualifying-examination marksheets, admission receipt, income certificate, domicile proof and bank details; the portal's checklist takes precedence. Applications are online through the official SVMCM portal. Recipients generally cannot simultaneously receive another central or state government scholarship or stipend for the same course or stage, subject to stated exceptions. AEC's 28 August 2025 notice identified nodal officers for the 2025-26 academic year. Confirm current rules and AEC's process.

question: What is the OASIS Post-Matric Scholarship for SC, ST and OBC students?
answer: The OASIS Post-Matric Scholarship provides financial assistance to eligible students from Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribe and Other Backward Class communities. Eligibility depends on the applicable category, domicile, course, income and other scheme requirements. The benefit varies by category, course level and current government rules, so there is no single fixed amount for all students. Documents may include a caste certificate, domicile or residence proof, income certificate, admission proof, marksheets and bank details, along with anything else requested by the portal. Applications are made through the official OASIS scholarship portal. Verify current category-specific income limits and amounts, and ask AEC's current nodal officer about the institution-side process.

question: What are the Aikyashree minority scholarship schemes?
answer: Aikyashree is a West Bengal scholarship programme for eligible minority-community students. Depending on the student's circumstances and current rules, possible schemes include the Post-Matric Scholarship, Merit-cum-Means Scholarship and Talent Support Programme. Eligibility depends on the relevant scheme's domicile, marks, income and course requirements. Benefits vary by scheme and course, so the current amount should be checked on the official portal. Required documents may include a minority-community declaration or certificate, marksheets, income certificate, admission proof and bank details. Applications are made through the West Bengal Minority Development and Finance Corporation scholarship portal. Minority students applying for SVMCM may have a dedicated process through the minority scholarship portal; follow the current portal's instructions and avoid duplicate applications.

question: What is the West Bengal Freeship Scheme (WBFS)?
answer: WBFS provides tuition-fee relief for eligible undergraduate students in engineering, technology, pharmacy and architecture at self-financing private institutions in West Bengal. Eligibility includes West Bengal domicile, a state or national entrance-exam merit rank and annual family income not exceeding ₹2.5 lakh. The benefit is a tuition-fee waiver; other fees remain payable. Students selected for AICTE's Tuition Fee Waiver (TFW) or SVMCM are not eligible for WBFS. Application windows are announced separately by the government. The PDF reports that the latest window it found was for 2024-25, with a deadline of 7 November 2025; an open 2026-27 window was not verified. Check the current notification.

question: What is the Tuition Fee Waiver (TFW)?
answer: TFW is a tuition-fee waiver mechanism associated with eligible engineering admissions, rather than a general cash scholarship. It aims to reduce the tuition-fee burden. Eligibility depends on the relevant admission authority, family-income requirements, rank and available TFW seats. Tuition fees are waived, but other charges may remain payable. Students generally need to meet the relevant admission and counselling rules and select or be allotted an eligible TFW seat. Not every student can request TFW after admission; confirm seat availability and the rules for the relevant admission year.

question: What is Nabanna or Chief Minister's Relief Fund educational assistance?
answer: Nabanna or Chief Minister's Relief Fund educational assistance provides financial support to eligible West Bengal students who need help continuing their studies. Published eligibility indicators include permanent residence in West Bengal, study at an eligible institution in the state, and marks within the scheme's specified ranges. The PDF describes 50% or more but less than 60% at Madhyamik or Higher Secondary level, or 50% or more but less than 53% in graduation for postgraduate assistance, depending on study level. The amount and approval depend on current relief-fund rules. Applications are made through the official Chief Minister's Relief Fund portal. A specific AEC institutional quota was not verified.

question: What is the National Scholarship Portal (NSP), and who should check its schemes?

question: What is the AICTE Swanath Scholarship?
answer: The AICTE Swanath Scholarship is intended for eligible students in specified vulnerable circumstances. Eligibility, approved-institution requirements and the current benefit must be checked in the relevant year's AICTE notification.

It is not a general scholarship for all students in West Bengal. Check the current scheme guidelines for eligibility, approved courses and application procedures.
